featured_reviews.name: Murtaza Anverali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kheema Pav Review: Heaven‑Level Street Fix

This is the version you tell people about: hot keema—fine‑grain mutton, tomatoes, green chili—heaped on a plate with butter‑licked pav maska toasted till the edges crunch. Special Chai arrives in a huge glass, milky‑sweet with ginger bite, just enough to cut the fat. You break pav, drag it through keema, sip chai, repeat. It’s messy, fast, and perfect at 8 am when the stall lights flick on. You really do have to eat it there to get the story. 10/10, no substitutes.

featured_reviews.name: Tomas Kramar
featured_reviews.review_text: Went here because it was recommended in the Dishoom book but felt very disappointed. Ordered bun maska with chai and we were served a stale crumbly brioche that the server picked up from a box, packaged in a plastic wrap. The bun looked like a burger bun and had little nibs of colorful jelly mixed in. The people around us were eating proper bun maskas with pav and it seemed to me that we have perhaps been served a bastardized version intentionally to cater to our foreign palates. I asked the waiter if we can get the same dish as the other guests were eating, but English was obviously a problem and we have just received the bill and the waiter cleaned the table. I hope this was just a misunderstanding, but if you are a western tourist, eat elsewhere.

Had the chance to visit Leopold Cafe and it truly feels like stepping into a piece of Mumbai’s history. Established in 1871, this iconic cafe carries a legacy that you can sense the moment you walk in—right from its vintage interiors to the buzzing, old-school charm.  ￼

The atmosphere is lively, slightly chaotic in the best way, and filled with a mix of locals and tourists from around the world. The walls, adorned with memorabilia and stories from the past, give the place a unique character that goes beyond just food.  ￼

The menu is extensive, offering everything from Indian to continental and Chinese dishes. The food is tasty and comforting, with generous portions, but the real highlight is enjoying a relaxed meal with a chilled drink while soaking in the vibrant Colaba vibe.  ￼

That said, it does get quite crowded, and you might have to wait for a table. Service can feel a bit rushed during peak hours, which is understandable given how popular the place is.  ￼

Overall, Leopold Cafe is less about fine dining and more about the experience, history, and atmosphere. It’s one of those places you visit not just for the food, but to truly feel the spirit of Mumbai. Definitely worth a visit at least once!

Leopold Cafe is one of Mumbai’s most iconic and historic cafés, known not just for its food but also for its deep connection with the city’s past. One of the most striking and emotional aspects of the place is that the gunshot marks from the 26/11 terror attack are still preserved, making it a powerful reminder of history and resilience.

The food and drinks are good in taste and reasonably priced compared to the location and popularity of the café. They offer a wide variety of options, including Indian, Continental, Chinese food, snacks, and beverages, making it suitable for all kinds of visitors. Portions are decent, and service is fairly quick considering the crowd.

The café is extremely crowded on weekends, especially in the evenings, so you may have to wait for a table. The atmosphere is lively, vibrant, and full of energy, attracting tourists, locals, and international visitors alike. The staff manages the crowd well and remains polite despite the rush.

Located in Colaba, it’s very close to major attractions like Gateway of India and is easy to reach. Overall, Leopold Cafe is a must-visit place in Mumbai for its history, legacy, lively vibe, and value-for-money food. A place you should experience at least once.

I discovered Araku Coffee during my stay in Mumbai, and it quickly became part of my daily routine.

Their Honey Oat Matcha is outstanding, and the food is just as good — especially the avocado toast, which I highly recommend.

Beyond the food and drinks, what really stands out is the space: clean, elegant, and full of natural light. It’s incredibly versatile — perfect for working on a laptop, unwinding with a book, or even hosting casual work meetings.

The staff deserve special mention: consistently friendly, welcoming, and highly professional. Always attentive and respectful, without ever being intrusive — a balance that’s not easy to achieve.

I honestly wish there were an Araku Coffee in Barcelona so I could keep coming back.

featured_reviews.name: WK
featured_reviews.review_text:
NICE PLACE, to enjoy coffee. This place is great for all special coffee lovers. From Hazelnut Latte to slow brewed coffee with natural chocolate ... Here you get them all. They also offer all these special coffee with different milk options. Regular, oat, coconut and almond milk. For the plant-based versions you have to pay.

The breakfast card is limited. Egg and bread lovers will find something but I missed a fresh fruit plate or a fresh salad. Also they don't offer fresh juice not even orange juice. Instead they have kombucha.
The price is ok and the service stuff is nice and friendly.

featured_reviews.name: Daddyslittlelunchbox
featured_reviews.review_text:
Araku was a really lovely spot and a nice change if you’re craving a continental-style breakfast. The café was clean, fresh, and well presented, with a calm and pleasant atmosphere that made it a comfortable place to sit and start the day.

Breakfast was decent and well prepared, with fresh flavours and good quality ingredients, although portions were on the smaller side. That said, everything felt light, fresh, and thoughtfully done, which made it a refreshing alternative to heavier breakfast options.

Overall, Araku is a great choice if you’re after something clean, simple, and fresh, and want a break from more traditional breakfast styles.

Follow us ➡️ @daddyslittlelunchbox

featured_reviews.name: Ebrahim Mukadam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a lovely experience at Araku. The vibe was warm, albeit slightly dimly lit for my lighting but yet I think the ambience was better than a lot of cafés around town.

Had a fish and rice and their pistachio cake for dessert. Both were in a league much better than what cafés serve.

I’d definitely go there again and try their coffee next time.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Vichare
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ 1/5 (Only because 0 stars isn’t an option)

Absolutely one of the worst breakfast experiences I’ve ever had.

We ordered two Kuckeliku Breakfast Platters — one with Pancakes & Yogurt Bowl and another with French Toast & Chia Seed Bowl. From the moment the food arrived, something felt seriously off.

The yogurt and chia bowls both had a strange smell and unpleasant taste. The sausages smelled stale, as if they had been sitting out for hours. The potatoes tasted and smelled like they had been cooked days ago and repeatedly reheated before being served.

The French toast looked completely unappetizing and honestly appeared unfit to eat. We didn’t even attempt to touch it. The pancakes were rubbery, dense, and served with what looked like a watery, glue-like syrup rather than anything resembling fresh pancake syrup.

For beverages, we ordered one hot latte and one cold latte. The hot latte was passable, but the cold latte looked like coffee-coloured water with almost no body, texture, or flavour.

The fried eggs were average at best, but the omelette was genuinely awful — soggy, wet, undercooked, and leaking liquid when cut into. It was difficult to believe it had passed any quality check before being served.

What was most alarming was the smell. Freshly prepared food usually has a pleasant aroma the moment it reaches the table. These platters did the exact opposite. The unpleasant smell was immediately noticeable and made the entire experience uncomfortable.

We informed the manager about the condition of the food, left almost everything untouched, paid the bill, and walked out.

What makes this experience even more disappointing is the amount we spent. We paid for a breakfast that was largely inedible. Leaving expensive food untouched because it simply wasn’t fit to eat is frustrating and feels like a complete waste of money.

I’ve attached photos so others can judge for themselves. Based on this experience, I would not recommend this place to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Ezel D
featured_reviews.review_text:
Used to be a preferred place for breakfast. However, this morning I was utterly disappointed since their standards have dropped beyond belief. The staff are no longer the same, badly behaved and the chef is clueless with their recipes. When poached eggs are served stone cold it's a place that can
be safely striked off from the list.

featured_reviews.name: Mayank
featured_reviews.review_text: The place is a vibe you can dwell in for hours. Pet friendly. The coffee is rejuvenating for the soul and the food is deliciously crafted with love. Lovely service 💯

featured_reviews.name: Andreas Michalis Loucas
featured_reviews.review_text:
H-O-R-R-I-B-L-E! & Expensive!!!
I dont get the good reviews at this place! It looks like a more western and clean place, but that is the only thing they offer. The service is polite, but at the same time not cut for the job. We ordered honey toast, waffles and a coffee. The americano took 10 minutes, the honey toast took 30 minutes and the waffles 40 minutes (FYI, we were only the second table in the store and the times were this long, cant imagine when they busy what happens). The honey toast presentation was like someone pooped on it, however, flavour was nice actually, BUT GUESS WHAT, the bread had mould lol. After finishing the toast, the waffles came that were not belgian as they say and was overcooked and it was like eating a cookie, we ordered banana on top, but have no idea what they put on but definitely it was not banana. HEAVILY HEAVILY on the overpriced side for india standards. Honestly stay away from this place, there something incredibly wrong with it.

featured_reviews.name: Janhvi Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text: We went for a small bite and ordered a yoghurt bowl and Greek coffee . The coffee was good .The yoghurt bowl was simple dahi with water like consistency. We asked why you serving liquid dahi instead of greek yogurt ? The person said this is what we serve … that’s it ….. they gave us chia seeds to add for consistency. Very disappointed with the service . They should simply write “ Dahi with berries “ and stop fooling people by writing “ yoghurt bowl “ which usually has greek yoghurt .

featured_reviews.name: Shilpaa Chogle
featured_reviews.review_text:
We reached Kuckeliku for a good breakfast & it wasn't good... it was great!!
The salmon latke was delicious, eggs Benedict perfectly done with spinach & salmon & the savoury waffle with chicken was yummy.  The Pineapple kale juice was fresh & coffee were amazing.
We had a fabulous experience!

featured_reviews.name: Kristen Dias
featured_reviews.review_text: It's the second time I've been and both were equally disappointing despite how much I wanted to enjoy it. The menu design is amazing and I'm sure the owners cooking would be fantastic, however it seems the execution of the chef on duty is not good at all. The prawns in the wrap weren't fresh. The filling in the lemon meringue cruffin was lumpy so I asked was it supposed to be lumpy, they offered to change it, when it came back it was still lumpy but also very thin. The waiter forgot half our order even though I asked him to repeat it back to me twice. Last time I ordered the 4 cheese grilled sandwich and the cheese was not melted at all. If it was executed as intended I'm sure it would be amazing but unfortunately this seems too much to expect. I won't go back a third time.

featured_reviews.name: Roslin Dwivedi
featured_reviews.review_text: It's a nice and quiet place for breakfast. We ordered the Kuckeliku breakfast set and got Pancakes, an omelette, potatoes, a Chia bowl, and sausages. We also ordered waffles, and we liked the breakfast there. The juices and smoothies are also very delicious. They have big teddy bears in the restaurant, which are very cute. And they kept one beside our son, which was a very nice gesture.

featured_reviews.name: Marlene Barnes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Churchill is one of those charming little places that proves great food doesn't need a fancy setting. Nestled in the heart of Colaba Causeway, this small, Parsi-run café has a warm, old-world charm and serves delicious, comforting food. Everything we ordered was excellent, but the standouts were definitely the Beef Teriyaki, Butter Garlic Beef Steak, and the Mixed Grill Lasagna. Each dish was packed with flavour, cooked perfectly, and served in generous portions. The food tasted fresh, hearty, and made with care. If you're looking for a cozy spot with authentic character, friendly service, and consistently good food, Cafe Churchill is well worth a visit. A true Colaba classic that keeps you wanting to come back for more!
PS: there is no parking available during peak hours.

featured_reviews.review_text: Good food with great hospitality. A bit cramped seating,though ...... But well, that's there for every Mumbai eatery.the lamb shank was really good. For the garlic bread, it was the normal pav bread with 🧄 c flavour. The icecream soda was one of a kind. Earlier ,we used to get these in Calcutta....not anymore. Location is prime ,hence parking might be an issue at times.

featured_reviews.name: Cassiee
featured_reviews.review_text:
The cafe of the month for me. The food was top-notch, brimming with flavour. From the delish Chicken Cordan Blue to the rich Tiramisu. A bit pricey but definitely a value for money in this economy.

Not only that, but the ambience and atmosphere, chefs kiss. Lovely old ladies, people from all around the world, fresh desserts being served and a mini crossword puzzle too! What an experience!

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Tipnis
featured_reviews.review_text:
A small eatery which is one of the older ones on Colaba Causeway. Right on the main street, it has barely 4-5 tables with minimal elbow room; but its USP is the wide variety of continental dishes including beef (buffalo meat only, since cow meat is banned in Maharashtra).

Tried their King Solomon Steak, but it was too well-done for my liking rendering it chewy - would've preferred it medium or medium-rare. The fish dish was quite good; overall do visit if you are a fan of non-Indian, non-Asian fare, and want a large no. of options to choose from.

Absolutely no parking available anywhere, so do use public transport (BEST Colaba Bus Depot / Electric House bus stop is just next to this restaurant) or cabs!

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Lovely restaurant in colaba. It's a small place with table sharing system on busy days. The sausages in firecracker sauce was our favorite, very juicy and flavourful.
The mixed grill lasagna was absolutely perfect, full of meat and cheat.
The beef(buff) teriyaki was top class, do not miss it. You'll clean the plate.
Crumb fried sausages were okay though, nothing special, you can skip it.

Next time we'll try the lamb chops and other dishes. Their overwhelming nenu has something for everyone. Can't wait to go again.

featured_reviews.name: Arif Faquih
featured_reviews.review_text: We were there to celebrate my friend’s birthday. The food was excellent, ambience was lively, and the hosts and their team were very courteous. Had a great time. The only downside was the place is very cramped up. Nevertheless we liked it and will visit again. Dr Arif & Dr Farida

featured_reviews.name: Harsh Saxena

Staff were a bit slow considering the amount of customers that were there. Pizza’s portion size was not upto the mark though.

A Hidden Gem by the Sea!

Had an absolutely wonderful experience at Bayview Café for lunch. The food was simply delicious; every dish was flavorful, well-prepared, and thoroughly enjoyable. While the prices are slightly on the higher side, the quality of the food, service, and overall experience make it completely worth it.

The service was top-notch, with attentive and courteous staff who made us feel welcome throughout our visit.

The café offers breathtaking views of the Arabian Sea and the iconic Gateway of India, making it a perfect spot to relax and unwind.

Convenience is another plus, with pay-and-park facilities available on the road. The rooftop seating area is easily accessible via an escalator, and for those visiting during the day, there is also a comfortable indoor air-conditioned section that's ideal for lunch.

Overall, Bayview Café offers the perfect combination of great food, stunning views, excellent service, and a memorable ambiance. A must-visit destination in Mumbai, whether you're planning a meal with family, friends, or even a special occasion.

Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited for dining at Bay View Cafe in Mumbai, and I must say it was good experience! Nestled along the stunning coastline, this cafe offers not only a delightful menu but also breathtaking views of the Arabian Sea.

From the moment we arrived, the ambiance set a perfect tone for our meal. The decor is charming and inviting, with a blend of modern and traditional elements that create a warm atmosphere. The outdoor seating area is particularly enchanting, allowing diners to soak in the sunset while enjoying their meals.

The menu at Bay View Cafe is diverse, featuring a variety of dishes that cater to different tastes. We started with some delicious appetizers, My friends enjoyed the pasta and vegetarian options.

One of the highlights of our visit was the exceptional service. The staff was attentive, friendly, and knowledgeable about the menu, making excellent recommendations. They truly went above and beyond to ensure we had a memorable dining experience.

Overall, Bay View Cafe is a gem in Mumbai that combines good food with stunning views. Whether you're looking for a romantic dinner, a family gathering, or just a place to unwind with friends, this cafe is a good option.

My recent dining experience was not very satisfactory. The place is quite expensive, and the portion sizes do not match the pricing. The food quality also did not meet expectations.

We ordered pesto pasta, but they did not serve even a single piece of garlic bread along with it. Usually, any standard café or restaurant provides at least one garlic bread with pasta, so this was disappointing.

We also ordered a brownie shake, but the shake had very little brownie in it. It tasted more like a basic chocolate shake with a lot of cream. Considering the price, the shake did not feel worth it.

Additionally, the restaurant charges a compulsory 7% service charge. However, there was no table service provided — the staff simply placed the food on the table and we had to serve ourselves. We ended up paying around ₹135 as service charge for just two dishes, which feels inappropriate.

Overall, I don’t think the dining experience is worth the price, and I would not recommend this place for dining.

featured_reviews.name: Anusuya
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Calm Vegetarian Haven in Kala Ghoda

Tucked away in the charming bylanes of the food area at Kala Ghoda Zen Cafe is a lovely vegetarian-only spot that offers a welcome break from the city's rush. The interiors are quaint with a warm relaxed vibe and the space is spread across two levels – a cosy ground floor and a quieter mezzanine level that’s perfect if you’re looking for a bit more privacy or calm.

The service is friendly and attentive which adds to the overall charm. The menu has plenty of interesting vegetarian options. We ordered the falafel wrap which was crunchy flavourful and left us wanting more. Light yet satisfying. The tomato pesto cheese sandwich was equally delicious – fresh and well made with comforting flavours.

And the cappuccino – really one of the highlights. Very very good. Smooth strong and creamy just the way a proper cappuccino should be.

Zen Cafe is the kind of place you’ll want to return to – for a peaceful solo break a quiet chat or simply to enjoy good food and coffee in a lovely tucked away corner of Kala Ghoda.

Food:

I had ordered, "Moroccan chickpea curry with rice" and I kid you not it was so delicious. It had that perfect home-cooked healthy meal vibe and to compliment it I had ordered fresh lime soda.

featured_reviews.review_text:
“Zen Café, Colaba- where calm meets craft.
Tried their veggie sushi roll, croissant with hot chocolate, and couldn’t help but admire the cozy rustic vibe. The space feels effortlessly artistic — warm lights, wooden textures, and the aroma of fresh bakes wrapping you in peace. A perfect corner for slow mornings, deep thoughts, and good food that speaks less and feels more.”

featured_reviews.name: Sakshi Lawand
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked away in the artsy lanes of Kala Ghoda, Zen Cafe is a quiet escape from the city's chaos, a minimalist, calming space perfect for slow mornings, work sessions, or thoughtful conversations. With natural light pouring in, wooden accents, and an almost meditative vibe, the ambiance lives up to the name “Zen.”

The menu leans towards healthy, vegetarian fare with Mediterranean and global influences. Their open sandwiches, hummus plates, and freshly baked goods are flavorful and light. Coffee is excellent, smooth and well-balanced, and the cold brews are especially worth a try. Portions are moderate, and presentation is clean and understated.

Prices are on the premium side, but you're paying for both quality and the peaceful setting, a rarity in South Mumbai. Service is polite and unhurried, which works well with the relaxed pace of the cafe.

A perfect spot to read, write, or simply slow down for a bit, Zen Cafe is a hidden gem for anyone who values good food in a beautiful, uncluttered space.

Mag St. at Apollo Bandar is easily one of the most enjoyable casual dining spots in South Mumbai right now. The space has a very relaxed yet polished energy, the service team is genuinely warm and efficient, and the overall experience feels extremely well thought out from start to finish.

A big plus in this part of Mumbai is that valet parking is available, which makes visiting far more convenient than most places nearby.

The food quality was outstanding across the board, fresh ingredients, clean flavors, excellent execution, and portions that feel fair for the pricing. Nothing felt gimmicky or overdone. Just really good food made with consistency and confidence. The menu strikes a smart balance between comfort and creativity.

What stood out most was how appropriately priced everything felt for the quality, location, and overall dining experience. In a city where many places are either overpriced or underwhelming, Mag St. manages to deliver genuine value.

Definitely a place worth revisiting, whether for coffee, brunch, or a relaxed meal with friends. Apollo Bandar needed a place like this.

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Trofima, Shivaji Park, Dadar, Mumbai

Cafe Trofima, located near the bustling Shivaji Park in Dadar, has garnered attention as a popular hangout spot, but it falls short of the hype for several reasons.

Food

The menu boasts a variety of food options, including breakfast platters, which might initially seem impressive. However, the taste of the food is compromised and does not justify the high prices. For a cafe that markets itself as a premium experience, the quality of the dishes leaves much to be desired.

Ambience and Seating

The sitting space is one of the better aspects of Cafe Trofima. Considering it is a cafe, the seating is comfortable and suitable for casual conversations or work. However, the overall ambience is just average, with no music to elevate the vibe. It lacks the warmth or charm that many would expect from a cafe in this area.

Service

The service is satisfactory but nothing extraordinary. While the staff is polite and attends to customers in a timely manner, the overall experience doesn’t stand out as memorable.

Location and Accessibility

A significant downside is the lack of parking space, which can be a hassle, especially given the busy location of Shivaji Park. Visitors arriving in their own vehicles may find it inconvenient.

Pricing

The prices are on the higher side, making it hard to justify for the quality of food and overall experience provided. While there are plenty of food options to choose from, the value for money is not reflected in the offerings.

Verdict

Cafe Trofima is overrated and doesn’t quite live up to its reputation. While it has some redeeming qualities like decent seating and satisfactory service, the compromised food taste, lack of parking, and high prices make it hard to recommend wholeheartedly. It could work as a one-time visit for those curious about its breakfast platters, but better options are available in and around the area for a more satisfying experience.

Overall Rating: 2/5

Their fresh sourdough and artisanal breads are absolute standouts and personal favourites—beautifully crusted, well-fermented, and full of character. The quiches and tarts are consistently satisfying, with buttery bases and well-balanced fillings that make them reliable picks every time. The tea cakes are another strong point: soft, moist, and understated, making them perfect companions to coffee or tea.

The pastry and cake counter is equally impressive, offering a wide range of flavours—from indulgent chocolate classics to lighter, nuanced options. Each dessert feels thoughtfully made, never overly sweet, and always well-executed. What’s equally commendable is the good balance of savoury items, which adds depth to the menu and keeps things interesting beyond desserts.

It’s the kind of place you return to not just for cravings, but for consistency, comfort, and the quiet joy of well-made food.

Nestled right beside the Tilak Bridge in Dadar-TT, you will find this small and cozy Irani restaurant that has been in continuous operation since 1934.
This establishment is a vital part of the city's rich history, representing a rapidly dwindling number of these legendary eateries.
An Authentic Vintage Experience.
Stepping inside is a truly transporting experience, offering a tangible journey back in time. The decor perfectly preserves the restaurant's old charm. You'll be surrounded by the unmistakable ambiance of a bygone era, complete with vintage bentwood chairs and large antique mirrors that reflect the passage of decades; Perfectly preserving classic Irani cafe aesthetic.

Kindly Note:
While this destination is highly recommended for its unique atmosphere and historical significance, please be aware that the restaurant maintains traditional practices and accepts cash payments only. Plan your visit accordingly to fully enjoy this piece of living history.

A friend recommended this Irani cafe, so I visited with my family, and it turned out to be a wonderful experience. We ordered kheema pav, bheja fry, and chicken cutlets  and every dish was absolutely delicious. The mutton kheema was full of rich flavors, so well cooked that we didn’t even need the usual onion and lemon on the side. The bheja fry was equally tasty, perfectly spiced and authentic.
The chicken cutlets deserve a special mention  crispy, juicy, and simply irresistible. My son loved them so much, which made the meal even more enjoyable for us.
We ended our meal with classic bun maska pav and Irani tea pure comfort and nostalgia. Words really fall short to describe how good it was.
The ambience truly adds to the charm of the place. It has a traditional Irani cafe design slightly old fashioned yet classic, giving a warm, nostalgic vibe that makes you feel connected to the heritage.
One more lovely thing about this place is the owner  extremely kind, polite, and well spoken, which adds a very personal and welcoming touch to the overall experience. I even clicked a photo to keep the memory of this visit.
Just a small thing to note , the cafe accepts cash only, so it’s better to carry cash as digital payments like GPay aren’t available.
Overall, an excellent place for authentic Irani cafe food with great hospitality. Highly recommended, and I would definitely love to visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
On a rainy Sunday, I had the pleasure of visiting **Café Colony**, a charming Irani café located in Hindu Colony, Dadar. The weather itself was perfect for the experience, as the comforting aroma of freshly brewed tea and baked bread created a warm, nostalgic atmosphere. The café has that classic Irani charm, with its simple yet inviting interiors that make you feel at home the moment you step in.

I began with their famous **Irani chai and brun maska**, and it was everything I had hoped for. The chai was strong, perfectly balanced with milk and sugar, and paired beautifully with the soft-yet-crispy brun generously slathered with butter. It was the kind of combination that instantly lifts your mood on a rainy day. Next, I tried the **keema fry with pav**, which turned out to be another highlight of the visit. The keema was spiced just right—rich, hearty, and bursting with authentic flavor—while the pav was fresh and fluffy, making it a wholesome and satisfying dish.

To end the meal on a sweet note, I indulged in their famous **gaz sweet**, a delicacy that lived up to its reputation. Its unique taste and texture added a perfect finishing touch to the experience, leaving me with a lasting impression of the café’s culinary heritage.

What made the visit even more special was the interaction with the lady owner of Café Colony. She was warm, courteous, and genuinely interested in knowing how we enjoyed the food. During our conversation, I shared that I am from Delhi and thoroughly enjoyed experiencing these authentic Irani dishes in Mumbai. Her hospitality, combined with the food, made the outing truly memorable.

Overall, Café Colony is not just about food—it’s about warmth, tradition, and conversations. A must-visit gem in Dadar.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Pirates Cafe, Borivali West with family and unfortunately had one of the most disappointing café experiences in recent times.

We ordered Coconut Cream Matcha, Special Thandai Ice Latte Signature, Cold Coffee Signature Tiramisu, Cold Coffee Café Mocha (Cold), Parmesan & Roasted Garlic Fries, along with other beverages. The drinks were average at best, while the fries were decent but nowhere close to compensating for the poor service experience.

The biggest issue was the attitude of the management. We were initially seated in the open-air section and requested a table in the AC section. However, once our order had been placed, there was absolutely no effort from the owners to accommodate the request. It felt as though, after securing the order, customer comfort became irrelevant.

The tables provided were also problematic. Two tables of different dimensions had been joined together, and both were continuously shaking because of uneven bases. Such basic maintenance issues reflect poorly on the attention given to customer experience.

What made the visit even more frustrating was the serving sequence. We ordered multiple beverages and fries together, expecting a family coffee outing where everyone could enjoy their orders at the same time. Instead, every item arrived separately with gaps of around five minutes. By the time the last beverage arrived, the first few drinks had already been consumed. This completely defeated the purpose of visiting a café as a group.

The staff appeared more focused on pleasing the owners than on delivering good customer service. Genuine hospitality was missing, and customer concerns were clearly not a priority.

To add to the irony, a table in the AC section was finally offered only when the last beverage was being served. It came across as artificial courtesy and fake empathy rather than a sincere attempt to resolve the issue.

Overall, an extremely bad experience. There are plenty of cafés that understand customer comfort, service quality, and hospitality far better than this place.

My rating reflects the attitude of the owners towards customers.

Looking at this review and rating, I expect the owners may respond with sympathy and explanations, but what customers need is better service and genuine concern, not post-review damage control.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Pibati is a charming little find for anyone who enjoys thoughtfully curated vegetarian food and well-made coffee. What instantly stands out is that the entire menu is 100% vegetarian, which is a big plus for people who specifically look for veg-friendly cafés without compromise on flavours or creativity.

We ordered quite a spread, starting with the Masala Avocado Toast, which was fresh, flavourful, and perfectly spiced without overpowering the natural taste of avocado. The Raw Papaya & Mango Bhel was a refreshing surprise — a lovely mix of crunch, tang, and sweetness that worked beautifully as a light starter. The Tadka Hummus had a desi twist and paired nicely with the accompaniments. For mains, the Aglio Olio Pasta was comforting, well cooked, and balanced in flavour. To finish, we enjoyed the Tiramisu Coffee and a Classic Cappuccino — both were satisfying and well brewed. We wanted to try their Matcha offerings, but we didn't order once they told us they still don't use Bree Matcha as their source of Matcha & we didn't want to risk having a bad Matcha experience.

Every dish we ordered tasted good, though the serving sizes could definitely be a little more generous, especially considering the pricing. One unique and interesting find was the Ghee Roast Croissant, which stood out for its creativity and flavour.

Seating-wise, the café has a small indoor area that accommodates around 15 people with roughly 6 compact tables, so it can feel a bit tight during peak hours. The outdoor seating is designated for smokers, so it’s best avoided if you’re visiting with kids. The service was prompt and courteous, which added to the overall positive experience.

Unfortunately, we were extremely hungry and only managed to click photos of the avocado toast before everything else arrived! Overall, Cafe Pibati is a great stop for vegetarian food lovers looking for quality food, good coffee, and a cozy café vibe — just with slightly limited seating and portion sizes. ✅☕🥑

In fact, another table cleared up just a couple of minutes after this conversation, and no new customer occupied that space for the rest of the time I was there.
